compounds.reasoning: A large flexible peptidomimetic bearing a thiazole ring, a thiazolylmethyl carbamate, and two benzyl groups (strongly reminiscent of the ritonavir scaffold) gives ample lipophilic bulk plus a heme-coordinating heteroaromatic nitrogen.

Contains a furan, an aminopyridine, a cyanoindole, and a fused pyrazolopyrimidine in one extended polyaromatic, multi-nitrogen system, giving both heme-coordinating pyridine-type nitrogens and a large planar stacking surface.

A fluorophenyl-piperidine linked through an ether to a benzodioxole has only a basic aliphatic secondary amine (not an aromatic heme-coordinating nitrogen) and modest overall aromatic bulk, so binding-pocket affinity is limited.

Small, fairly polar molecule (hydroxy-propanamide, piperidine, indazole-NH) with low aromatic surface area and no strong heme-coordinating nitrogen, so it falls below typical CYP3A4-inhibitor lipophilicity/size.

A small dichlorobenzyl amine with cyclopropyl and azetidine groups has only one aromatic ring and a simple aliphatic amine, lacking the bulk and heme-binding nitrogen needed for strong CYP3A4 affinity.

A dimethoxyphenyl-pyrrolidinone N-substituted with an OCF3-benzyl group is moderately lipophilic with two aromatic rings, but the lactam nitrogen's lone pair is delocalized into the carbonyl and there is no azole/pyridine heme-coordinating nitrogen.

A large tricyclic purine/pyrimido-indole aromatic core with multiple ring nitrogens (kinase-inhibitor-like scaffold) plus a flexible alkylamino tail provides both a heme-coordinating diazine nitrogen and extensive planar stacking surface.

This is a macrolactone with multiple sugar rings and a tertiary amine, structurally matching the erythromycin/roxithromycin macrolide class, which is a well-known, mechanism-based strong CYP3A4 inhibitor family.

Contains a benzimidazole (fused imidazole, heme-coordinating nitrogen), an aminopyridine substituent, and a chlorophenyl-thiophene carboxamide, combining an azole-type nitrogen with substantial aromatic/halogen lipophilicity.

A difluoromethylpyridine linked to a fused triazolo-naphthyridine-type polyaromatic system offers multiple sp2 nitrogens (pyridine and triazole) for heme coordination along with an extensive flat aromatic stacking surface.

An imidazolylmethyl group (classic heme-coordinating azole nitrogen) attached near a fluorinated biphenyl amide gives moderate lipophilic aromatic bulk plus the type II inhibition signal, though the molecule is otherwise fairly compact.

A CF3/ethyl-substituted fused bicyclic aromatic lactam with a piperazine has only a basic aliphatic NH (no azole/pyridine nitrogen) and a relatively small ring system, limiting deep hydrophobic-pocket engagement.

A guanidine-carboxamide (highly polar, likely protonated at physiological pH) attached to a piperidine-cyclopropanecarbonyl and a CF3-phenyl is dominated by polar/basic character rather than lipophilicity, with no heme-coordinating azole nitrogen.

A methoxypiperidine-substituted benzimidazole fused to a pyridinone bearing a chlorophenyl-hydroxyethylamino arm is a large, multi-ring heteroaromatic (kinase-inhibitor-like) structure with heme-coordinating benzimidazole nitrogens and extensive conjugation.

Two pyridine-type diazine rings (each with a lone-pair nitrogen) connected by an ether and a chloropyridyl amide give some heme-coordination potential, but the molecule is relatively small and polar overall, keeping affinity borderline.

A heavily halogenated (four Cl plus F) indole-acrylamide-sulfonamide-dichlorothiophene assembly has very high lipophilicity and a large planar polyaromatic surface, even though the indole nitrogen is alkylated and unavailable for heme coordination.

This dioxolane bearing an imidazole and a 2,4-dichlorophenyl group, linked via an aryl ether to a piperazine-thiophenesulfonyl moiety, is essentially the ketoconazole/itraconazole azole-antifungal pharmacophore, the textbook example of type II CYP3A4 heme-nitrogen inhibition.

A triazolone plus a tetrazole attached to a tertiary alcohol flanked by di/mono-fluorophenyl rings closely mirrors the fluconazole/voriconazole triazole-antifungal design, a classic heme-nitrogen-coordinating CYP3A4 inhibitor motif.

A tricyclic ether-bridged benzoxazinone-sulfonamide-fluorobenzo system provides notable fused aromatic surface area, but lacks any azole/pyridine heme-coordinating nitrogen and carries polar lactam/sulfonamide groups that offset lipophilicity.

A cyanoguanidine (highly polar, H-bond-heavy, cimetidine-like) connected through a flexible hexyl-chlorophenoxy chain to a pyridylamine provides one heme-coordinating pyridine nitrogen, but the dominant cyanoguanidine polarity works against strong CYP3A4 binding.

A pyridin-3-yl group directly bonded to the piperidine's tertiary aryl-amine nitrogen sits alongside a CF3-phenyl and isoxazole, giving a heme-coordinating pyridine N plus substantial lipophilic bulk.

Carries both a 1,2,3-triazole and a 1,2,4-oxadiazole on adjacent aromatic rings plus a chlorophenyl and morpholine, the classic azole-type-II heme-ligation motif combined with high aromatic lipophilicity.
A pyrazole linked to a pyridylmethyl amide and a pyrimidine bearing a thiophene gives several sp2 nitrogens capable of heme coordination in a moderately lipophilic, multi-ring scaffold.

Small dichlorophenyl attached to a saturated azabicyclic amine with no conjugation between the basic nitrogen and any aromatic/heteroaromatic pi system, so there is no heme-coordinating geometry and low overall bulk.

Fused imidazo-pyridine (two ring nitrogens) plus a bromo-enone spiro-cyclohexane and pendant phenyl make this a large, highly lipophilic polyheteroaromatic capable of active-site stacking and heme approach.
Near-identical triazole/oxadiazole/morpholine pharmacophore to other azole-bearing analogs in this set, with an added dimethylphenyl increasing lipophilicity.
A trichlorinated diarylamide is lipophilic but its only nitrogen is a tertiary amide whose lone pair is delocalized into the carbonyl, giving poor heme-iron ligation capacity.

A large, flexible molecule combining a planar chromone, a dimethoxybenzamide, and a pyrazole-fused indazolylpiperidine offers extensive aromatic surface and lipophilic bulk that fits a large hydrophobic CYP3A4 pocket well.

A biphenyl-linked aminopyrazole with free aniline and phenol groups is reasonably planar/aromatic but carries multiple polar H-bond donors that reduce net lipophilicity and lack a classic heme-coordinating azole nitrogen.

A large dihydroisoquinolinone core bearing a chlorophenyl, a tertiary benzylic amine, and a piperazinone gives substantial lipophilic bulk and multiple basic/aromatic nitrogens well suited to the flexible CYP3A4 pocket.

This is a macrolide-type macrocyclic lactone with a desosamine-like sugar, cyclic carbamate/imine nitrogen, and tertiary amine — the structural class typified by erythromycin/clarithromycin that is a canonical mechanism-based CYP3A4 inhibitor.

A lignan-lactone (podophyllotoxin-like) scaffold with methoxy/hydroxy-substituted aromatic rings has no basic or heme-coordinating nitrogen at all, limiting inhibition potential despite moderate aromaticity.
Contains an isoquinoline nitrogen, a pyridin-3-yl group, and a piperazine linker within a large dimethoxy-diamide scaffold, giving multiple heme-ligating nitrogens plus high lipophilic bulk.

A biphenyl-cyclohexyl system is lipophilic and aromatic-rich, but the free carboxylic acid on the cyclopropane will be ionized at physiological pH, disfavoring deep partition into the hydrophobic active site and removing any heme-coordinating nitrogen.
A polar hydroxamic acid and sulfonamide flank a pyrimidine-linked bicyclic amine and naphthalene, giving one heme-coordinating pyrimidine nitrogen but substantial polarity that likely limits potency.

Essentially a fluorinated biphenyl with a gem-dimethylcyclohexane and a cyclobutane carboxylic acid — lipophilic ring system but again terminates in an ionizable acid with no heme-ligating nitrogen present.

A chloropyridine ether tethered through a piperidine to a pyrrolidine-acetic acid, with extended ether/alkyl chains, provides a heme-coordinating pyridine nitrogen and considerable flexible lipophilicity, partly offset by the terminal carboxylic acid.

Two separate pyridine rings (one bearing chlorine, one bearing fluorine) connected through an ether and an amide give multiple sp2 nitrogens available for heme coordination despite modest overall size.

A very large, highly lipophilic molecule combining a tetrahydroisoquinoline, a 1,2,3-triazole, a pyridyl ether, and a planar chromone amide gives multiple heme-coordinating nitrogens plus extensive aromatic surface for the spacious CYP3A4 pocket.
Shares the triazole + oxadiazole + morpholine + chloro/fluorophenyl pharmacophore seen in related analogs, a strong azole-type heme-ligation signal combined with high lipophilicity.
An imidazole ring hangs directly off the core arene alongside a phenyl-pyrazine amide, giving a classic heme-coordinating azole N plus extended planar aromatic surface.
A large flexible peptidomimetic (protease-inhibitor-like) bearing two thiazoles, two benzyl phenyls and a pyrrolidine urea is bulky, lipophilic and rich in coordinating N.
Benzoxazole and thiazole rings combined with a cyclohexylmethyl amide and benzyl carbamate give a large, lipophilic, N-heterocycle-laden scaffold typical of strong 3A4 binders.
A chloropyridine directly linked to a pyridine core plus a 2-pyridyl substituent creates a bipyridine-like heme-chelating motif on an otherwise moderately lipophilic scaffold.
A stilbene-like biaryl bearing chlorine, an imidazole, a trifluoromethoxyphenyl sulfonamide and a piperazine is large, highly halogenated/lipophilic, and carries a classic heme-binding azole N.
This is an enormous, highly lipophilic multi-ring venetoclax-like scaffold (spirocycle, piperidine, nitroarylsulfonamide, pyridoindole ether) that fills a large hydrophobic pocket easily.
A chlorophenyl-substituted dihydroisoquinolinone with a piperazinone-linked cyclohexyl aniline is moderately lipophilic and aromatic but lacks a strong heme-coordinating azole N.
A fused thienopyrimidinedione core carries a dichloro-methylimidazole substituent, giving both a heme-coordinating azole nitrogen and a halogenated, moderately planar polycyclic system.
Multiple fused N-heterocycles (furan-pyridine, indole, pyrazolopyrimidine) create an extended, nitrogen-dense planar aromatic system consistent with active-site stacking and heme access.
Two separate azole rings (a 1,2,3-triazole and a thiazole) each on aryl substituents give a strong double heme-coordination signal reminiscent of azole antifungal chemistry.
A methylenedioxyphenylacetamide linked to a thiazole-azaindole gives moderate lipophilicity and an azole/pyridine-type nitrogen but a relatively compact, non-bulky framework.
Heavy fluorination (CF3, aryl-F), a biphenyl-like phenyl-azaindole system and a bulky gem-dimethyl chain give high lipophilicity and an accessible pyridine-type nitrogen.
A bicyclic pyrimidinone core linked through a diarylamine to an oxadiazole-piperazine gives several coordinating nitrogens on a moderately large, kinase-inhibitor-like lipophilic scaffold.
A 1,3,4-thiadiazole fused to an azaindole via an acetamide provides adjacent heme-coordinating nitrogens, though the overall molecule is modestly sized and polar (sulfonamide).
An imatinib-like diaminopyrimidine/pyrrolopyridine core with a basic piperidine and isopropylsulfone aryl group is large, aromatic-N-rich and moderately lipophilic.
An imidazole tethered by a CH2 linker plus a fluorinated biphenylamide is only moderately sized and lipophilic, with the azole N not well positioned for direct heme access.
A pyrrolopyrimidine kinase-inhibitor-like core bearing a benzoxazole, cyclopentyloxy group and diarylamine linkage is large and rich in aromatic/heterocyclic nitrogen.
A pyrazolopyridine amide bearing a methylsulfonylpyridine and fluorophenyl group has multiple aromatic nitrogens but is moderate in size and polarity (sulfone).
A benzimidazole thioether linked to a cyclohexylmethyl group carries a genuine heme-coordinating fused-azole nitrogen, though the molecule itself is fairly small and only modestly lipophilic.
A trifluoromethylphenyl bearing both a triazole and a separate oxadiazole, plus a morpholine amide, combines two heme-coordinating azole rings with substantial lipophilicity.

Large flexible peptide-like macrocycle with a phenol, an indole-type aromatic, a benzyl urea and a tertiary piperazine nitrogen, giving substantial bulk and lipophilicity to fill the large CYP3A4 pocket.
A dimethoxyphenyl-chlorolactam bearing a benzylic OCF3 group is moderately lipophilic and halogenated but has no pyridine/azole nitrogen available to coordinate heme iron.

Four aromatic/heteroaromatic rings (isoxazole-amine bicycle, chlorophenyl, difluorophenyl, thiadiazole) linked by a diaryl ether and sulfonamide give large planar lipophilic surface area plus a thiadiazole nitrogen capable of heme coordination.
Contains both a 1,2,4-triazole and an oxadiazole ring attached to a biaryl fluorophenyl-methoxyphenyl scaffold, a classic multi-azole heme-iron-coordinating motif reminiscent of azole antifungals.
Same triazole+oxadiazole diazole pharmacophore fused to a fluorophenyl-morpholine amide with a dimethylphenyl group, giving strong heme-coordination potential and good lipophilicity.
Regioisomer of the previous triazole/oxadiazole-morpholine amide scaffold, retaining the dual-azole heme-binding motif and aromatic bulk.

Pyridylmethylpyridine ether with an aminochloropyridine amide provides several pyridine-type lone-pair nitrogens for heme coordination, though the molecule is relatively small and moderately polar overall.

A complex fused polycyclic scaffold containing a nitrile, diaryl ether, and an imidazole ring within a macrocyclic lactam offers both strong azole-type heme coordination and large lipophilic aromatic surface.
A methoxyphenylsulfonamide-pyrrolidine amide with a thioanisole substituent is moderately lipophilic but lacks any pyridine/azole nitrogen for heme-iron coordination, limiting inhibition risk.

A flexible peptidomimetic bearing a thiazole and an N-methylimidazole plus two benzyl/phenyl groups combines multiple azole heme-coordinating nitrogens with high lipophilicity, favoring the large CYP3A4 pocket.

An extended conjugated indazole-styryl system fused to a methoxy-spirocyclopropane indane, with a dimethylaminomethyl group, provides a large planar aromatic stacking surface plus a tertiary/indazole nitrogen.
An oxazolidinone/morpholinone core with a chlorothiophene amide and formamide is compact and polar (several carbonyls) with only amide-type nitrogens, unlikely to engage the heme iron strongly.

A biphenol-naphthalene-aniline system is a highly extended planar polyaromatic capable of active-site pi-stacking, though the multiple phenolic/amino groups add polarity that partly offsets lipophilicity.

A bromobenzyl urea linked to a purine-like fused pyrrolopyrimidine gives multiple heteroaromatic ring nitrogens (imidazole/pyridine-type) for heme coordination along with a halogen and extended aromatic surface.

A large macrocyclic kinase-inhibitor-like structure with a pyrazole, fused diazepine/pyrimidine, nitrile and long lipophilic ether tether presents ample heme-coordinating nitrogen and bulk to fill the CYP3A4 cavity.

A Hantzsch-type dihydropyridine bearing a chlorofluorophenyl substituent and an N-pyrazolylmethyl group resembles the dihydropyridine calcium-channel-blocker class known to interact with CYP3A4, giving moderate risk.

A butyl-methylurea piperidine conjugated through an enyne to a methylpyridine provides one heme-coordinating pyridine nitrogen plus moderate alkyl/alkyne lipophilicity, but overall bulk and aromaticity are limited.

A pyrimidinylacetamide-piperidine attached to a fused imidazo-fluorene tricyclic system offers both azole/pyrimidine nitrogen lone pairs for heme binding and an extended planar aromatic stacking surface.

A dioxolane bearing both an imidazole and a dichlorophenyl group attached to a piperazine sulfonamide closely mirrors the classic azole-antifungal (ketoconazole-like) pharmacophore, a strong type II heme-coordination signal.

A biaryl linking a morpholine-substituted amine to a fused dimethyl-quinoxalinone through an amide gives multiple aromatic rings and a fused heteroaromatic bicycle, contributing notable lipophilic bulk though coordinating nitrogens are mostly amide-type.

Large flexible molecule with a tertiary amine linker, tetrahydroisoquinoline, and a fused pyridine (cccnc) capable of heme-iron coordination, plus high overall lipophilicity from the gem-dimethyl cyclohexane and multiple aromatic rings.

Peptidomimetic scaffold (protease-inhibitor-like) with a thiazole nitrogen, carbamate, and two benzyl groups giving large lipophilic surface area typical of classic potent CYP3A4 inhibitors like ritonavir.
Biaryl pyridine core with a piperazine and a CF3-substituted aromatic ring gives moderate lipophilicity and a heme-coordinating pyridine nitrogen embedded in an extended planar system.

Contains three separate pyridine-type nitrogens connected by an ether and amide linkage, a strong heme-coordination signal, though the molecule is relatively small and fluorinated, limiting hydrophobic pocket fill.
Fused tetrahydroisoquinoline-pyridine system with a cyclopropylpiperazine and tertiary amine, closely resembling compound 1's flexible lipophilic pharmacophore with a heme-coordinating pyridine.
Methoxypyridine plus an indole and a free phenyl ring around a ketone gives an extended, moderately lipophilic aromatic system with a heme-coordinating pyridine nitrogen.
Fused xanthine/thienopyrimidinedione core bearing a quinoline-type nitrogen and a pyrrolidinol amide; sizeable planar heteroaromatic system but tempered by polar carbonyl/hydroxyl groups.

Bears both an oxadiazole and a 1,2,3-triazole ring alongside a fluorophenyl and morpholine amide -- triazoles are the classic azole-antifungal CYP3A4 heme-ligating motif despite the morpholine's polarity.
Large macrolide lactone with an aminosugar and a pyridylpropyl carbamate substituent -- structurally analogous to erythromycin/clarithromycin, prototypical potent CYP3A4 mechanism-based inhibitors.

Highly flexible bis-tertiary-amine chain flanked by a tetrahydroisoquinoline-pyridine fusion and a separate pyridylmethyl group, giving multiple heme-coordinating nitrogens and substantial lipophilic bulk.
Polycyclic fused benzoxazole/quinazolinedione-like system with a methoxy group and a hydantoin-bearing benzyl arm gives a large planar aromatic surface favorable for the CYP3A4 pocket.

Minimal biaryl of pyridine and thiophene with no other substituents -- despite a heme-coordinating pyridine nitrogen, the molecule is too small and simple to effectively fill the large hydrophobic pocket.

Extended naphthalene-diphenol (stilbene/flavonoid-like) aromatic system offers large planar stacking surface typical of flavonoid CYP3A4 inhibitors, moderated somewhat by the polar sulfonamide and phenols.
Bulky, flexible molecule with piperazine, piperidine, biphenyl, and a fluorophenyl ketone providing substantial lipophilic surface for the large CYP3A4 cavity, even without a classic azole nitrogen.
Densely fused pyrazolo-pyrimidine core plus separate pyridine, indole, and furan rings creates an extensively conjugated polyheteroaromatic system rich in heme-coordinating nitrogens.
Trihydroxyflavone (chromone) scaffold -- flavonoids of this type are well documented CYP3A4 inhibitors via planar aromatic stacking, though the polyhydroxylation adds polarity.
Carries both a 1,2,3-triazole and a thiazole nitrogen alongside a morpholine amide and phenyl substituents, giving two classic azole-type heme-ligating groups on a moderately lipophilic scaffold.
Sulfonamide-thiazole with a chloro/fluorophenyl and an N-hydroxypiperidine is comparatively small and polar (sulfonamide, N-OH), limiting hydrophobic pocket engagement despite the thiazole nitrogen.
Pyrazole-containing molecule with cyclopentyl, a bicyclic spiro amine, and two separate phenyl rings gives notable steric bulk and lipophilicity favorable to the large CYP3A4 active site.
Fused benzimidazole-thiophene core plus a separate aminopyridine and chlorophenyl group provides multiple heme-coordinating nitrogens on an extended, fairly lipophilic aromatic scaffold.

A pentynyl-fluorophenyl/difluoromethoxy-tolyl hydantoin-guanidine is lipophilic with several aryl/halogen groups but the only nitrogens are an amidine-type guanidine, not a classic heme-coordinating azole/pyridine lone pair.

A biaryl (fluoroanisole-pyridine) linked via an ether to a cyclobutyl isothiocyanate has a pyridine nitrogen that could weakly coordinate heme iron but overall modest bulk and polarity from the isothiocyanate keep lipophilicity moderate.

A dichlorobenzamide N-aryl(chlorophenyl) with a pendant primary aminoethyl group is fairly lipophilic and halogenated but the free primary amine is a poor heme ligand and there is no azole/pyridine nitrogen, giving only moderate risk.

This bulky compound bears two separate triazole rings plus a phenyl and cyclopentyl/spirocyclic cage, and triazole nitrogens are classic azole-type heme-iron ligands combined with high overall lipophilic bulk.

An extended fused pyrazolo-pyridine core linked through a urea to a phenethylamine-pyridine carries multiple sp2 nitrogen lone pairs (pyrazole, pyridine) on a fairly planar polyaromatic scaffold, favoring heme coordination and pocket stacking.

A dimethoxyphenyl-substituted pyrrolidinone N-benzylated with a trifluoromethoxyphenyl group is moderately lipophilic but its only nitrogen is an amide within the lactam, which is a poor heme-iron ligand.

This molecule combines a triazole, a fused imidazo-pyridazine-like bicyclic heteroaromatic, a tetrafluorophenoxy group, and a butyl chain, giving strong heme-coordinating azole/aza-aromatic nitrogens plus high overall lipophilic bulk.

A polychlorinated diaryl ether sulfonanilide with an acetylpyridine is highly halogenated and lipophilic with a pyridine-type nitrogen available for weak heme coordination, though it is substituted and somewhat hindered.

A fluorocinnamamide bearing a morpholine and fluorophenyl group is only modestly lipophilic and its nitrogens are an amide and a morpholine ether-amine, neither a strong heme-iron ligand nor part of an extended planar aromatic system.

A chloropyridine-piperidine linked via a diaryl ether to a trifluoromethyl-pyrazoline acetic acid is structurally complex and lipophilic with a pyridine nitrogen present, giving moderate heme-coordination potential.

This fused benzimidazole/pyridinone scaffold carries a morpholine and an additional imidazole-bearing side chain, giving multiple classic azole-type nitrogens on an extended planar heteroaromatic system that favors both heme coordination and pocket stacking.

A fused benzimidazole-pyridinone core substituted with a free imidazole ring and a pyridylmethyl group presents several strong heme-iron-coordinating azole/pyridine nitrogens on a large planar aromatic system, a textbook CYP3A4 pharmacophore.

This molecule contains both a 1,2,4-triazole and an oxadiazole ring plus chloro- and fluorophenyl groups linked through a morpholine amide, combining multiple azole-type heme-coordinating nitrogens with substantial halogenated aromatic bulk.

A tricyclic purine/pyrimido-indole-like aromatic core with an aminopyrimidine and extended fused ring system, substituted with flexible alkyl-alcohol and tetrahydrofuranylmethyl amine chains, presents a large planar heteroaromatic surface with multiple ring nitrogens capable of active-site interaction.

Identical structure to the previous entry: a tricyclic purine/pyrimido-indole-like aromatic core with an aminopyrimidine and extended fused ring system, substituted with flexible alkyl-alcohol and tetrahydrofuranylmethyl amine chains, giving a large planar heteroaromatic surface with multiple ring nitrogens.

A cyclohexylamine tethered via an ethylamine to a chloro/fluoro-aminobenzenesulfonamide bearing an aminothiazole has a thiazole nitrogen for weak heme coordination but otherwise moderate lipophilicity and a polar sulfonamide limiting binding.

Identical structure to the previous entry: a cyclohexylamine-ethylamine linked to a chloro/fluoro-aminobenzenesulfonamide bearing an aminothiazole, with a thiazole nitrogen offering weak heme coordination but moderate overall lipophilicity.

A pyrazole-substituted benzamide fused to a difluoro-tetrahydrobenzazepine bearing a pyridylmethyl amide and a chlorophenyl group is large, lipophilic, and richly polyaromatic with multiple heterocyclic nitrogens well suited to the CYP3A4 pocket.

This compound has a fused triazole-oxazine bicyclic system plus a separate free imidazole ring, a trifluoromethylphenyl, and a methoxyphenyl group, giving multiple strong azole heme-coordinating nitrogens on a lipophilic polyaromatic scaffold.

An aminopyrazole fused to a triazole/tetrazole-like bicyclic heterocycle, connected through a pyrazole-methylene linker to a phenylpiperidine, offers several azole nitrogens but the molecule is fairly polar overall with a free amine, moderating lipophilicity.

Large flexible peptidomimetic with two benzyl groups, a thiazole ring, and a thiazolylmethyl carbamate offering multiple weak heme-coordinating N atoms in a high-logP scaffold reminiscent of HIV protease inhibitors.
Fused pyrazolo-triazine core bearing a CF3 group, phenyl substituent and methoxyphenyl provides an extended planar aromatic system with adjacent sp2 nitrogens, favoring active-site stacking.
A thienopyrimidine fused heteroaromatic core linked to a sulfonamide-bearing benzylpiperidine gives a large planar N-rich aromatic surface with strong heme-coordination potential.
Trisubstituted pyridine diaryl ether with a dichlorophenylsulfonamide combines a heme-coordinating pyridine nitrogen with heavy halogenation, raising lipophilicity and active-site affinity.
Nitrile-substituted diaryl ether featuring a chloropyridine and dichlorobenzenesulfonamide again places a coordinating pyridine N in a halogen-rich lipophilic biaryl framework.

A hydroxypyrrolidine amide linked through a phenyl to an oxadiazole and cyclohexylethyl chain is moderately lipophilic but the oxadiazole N is poorly positioned and the molecule lacks an extended planar aromatic surface.

A bulky adamantane-like tricyclic cage fused to a dimethoxy-tetrahydroisoquinoline amide and methyl benzoate gives very high lipophilicity and bulk that fits the large CYP3A4 pocket, with a tertiary amine as weak coordinator.

A large flexible bis-carbamate peptidomimetic bearing a pyridylmethyl tertiary amine plus two thiazole rings and multiple phenyls presents strong heme-coordination potential in a very lipophilic scaffold.
Fused benzimidazole-pyridinone kinase-inhibitor-like scaffold with a dimethylaminopiperidine and chlorophenyl carbinol offers several coordinating nitrogens on an extended aromatic system.

A fluorophenylpyrazole carboxamide bearing a free carboxylic acid is moderately sized but the ionizable acid group lowers effective lipophilicity and active-site binding despite the pyrazole nitrogens.

A fluorobenzoylpiperidine bearing an N-aryl pyridine with a trifluoromethylphenyl substituent has a heme-coordinating pyridine nitrogen embedded in a highly lipophilic multi-aromatic, halogenated framework.

Close analog of the previous compound with a benzoylpiperidine, chlorophenyl and pyridine substituent, retaining the coordinating pyridine N and multi-ring lipophilicity though slightly less halogenated.
An imidazole ether flanked by two methoxyphenyl groups closely resembles the classic azole-antifungal pharmacophore, a strong type II heme-iron-coordination signal.

An extended fused aminopyridine-triazanaphthalene system carrying a phenyl and an aminocyclobutylphenyl group is a large planar polyaromatic, N-heterocyclic scaffold well suited to the roomy CYP3A4 pocket.

A brominated quinoline fused with a methylenedioxyphenyl and bearing a tertiary dimethylaminoethyl chain and pyridine ring is a bulky, highly lipophilic, halogenated polyaromatic amine reminiscent of antimalarial quinolines known to inhibit CYP3A4.
An imidazolylacetate ester linked to a fluorophenyl-phenyl biaryl amide again places an imidazole heme-coordinating nitrogen on a lipophilic biaryl scaffold.
Large flexible urea-linked peptidomimetic bearing a thiazole ring, a second thiazolylmethyl carbamate and two phenyl groups gives strong heme-coordination potential in a very high-logP molecule.

A pyrrolopyrimidine (purine-like) fused heteroaromatic linked via an amine to a piperidine acetamide bearing a dichlorophenyl group combines multiple coordinating ring nitrogens with halogen-driven lipophilicity.

A purine-like fused triazolopyrimidine directly conjugated to a chlorophenyl-piperidine gives an electron-rich fused N-heteroaromatic well positioned for heme iron coordination alongside notable lipophilicity.

Near-identical scaffold to the first compound (secondary methylamine in place of the acetamide) retaining the two thiazole rings, carbamate and multiple phenyls, so the same strong high-logP heme-coordination risk applies.

Candesartan/ARB-like scaffold with an ethoxy-benzimidazole (aromatic sp2 N available for heme coordination) fused to a lipophilic biphenyl-tetrazole system that stacks well in a large hydrophobic pocket.
Contains an N-aryl 1,2,4-triazole plus an oxadiazole and a methoxy-biaryl core, giving both a heme-coordinating azole nitrogen and extended aromatic surface for pocket stacking.
Small aminomethyl-pyridine ether bearing a fluoro-hydroxypyrrolidine amide; the pyridine N is ether-flanked and the molecule is compact and polar (free NH2, OH, amide) with low overall lipophilicity.

Bulky multi-ring system (2,5-disubstituted oxazole, phenyl ether, tert-butylphenyl amide) offers a large lipophilic/aromatic surface, but a free carboxylic acid ionizes at physiological pH and blunts heme access, giving mixed risk.

N-methylpiperidine tethered through an aminoethyl linker to a chloro/fluoroaniline sulfonamide-thiazole, combining a basic sp3 amine and an aromatic thiazole N with two halogens for added lipophilicity.

Large fused polyheterocyclic core (imidazo-fused pyridine/pyrrolopyridine) decorated with a methylisoxazole and tetrahydropyran, giving an extended planar aromatic system rich in ring nitrogens well suited to the CYP3A4 cavity.
Pyrazolopyridine core with a dimethylpyridine and a phenylethyl urea; several pyridine-type nitrogens exist but the urea and NH groups add polarity that partially offsets the moderate aromatic bulk.

Heavily chlorinated diaryl ether/sulfonamide (four Cl atoms) with a pyridine nitrile core, giving high lipophilicity, an accessible pyridine N, and extensive aromatic surface — classic promiscuous CYP3A4 substrate features.

N-aryl triazole on a chlorophenyl ring combined with a morpholine amide and an oxadiazole-phenyl group provides a heme-coordinating azole plus multiple aromatic rings, though morpholine polarity moderates overall lipophilicity.

Fused pyrrolopyridine (7-azaindole-like) bearing a fluorophenyl and a pyridin-4-ylamino substituent gives an extended planar heteroaromatic system with multiple nitrogens capable of heme coordination, typical of kinase-inhibitor-class CYP3A4 hits.

N-methyltetrazole-methyl chloropyridine linked to a dichlorophenyl sulfonamide; tetrazole nitrogens offer weaker heme-coordination than imidazole/triazole, and the sulfonamide adds polarity despite three chlorines boosting lipophilicity.

Biaryl thiophene linking two phenols (methylphenol and hydroxyphenyl); no basic or heme-coordinating nitrogen, and the two free phenolic OH groups add polarity/H-bonding that reduces net lipophilicity.

Nitrogen-rich molecule combining a benzyl-tetrazole, an aryl-1,2,4-triazole, and a cyclobutyl-piperazine tertiary amine — multiple azole/basic nitrogens plus substantial aromatic and alicyclic bulk favor pocket binding and heme access.
Isoxazole-carboxamide bridging two chlorophenyl rings; the isoxazole N sits adjacent to ring oxygen (weaker heme ligand than imidazole/triazole) and the molecule is only moderately sized/lipophilic.

Large tetracyclic aminopyrimidine-indole/carbazole-type scaffold (PI3K-inhibitor-like) with an extended planar fused aromatic system and multiple pyrimidine/indole nitrogens, strongly favoring stacking and heme coordination in the large CYP3A4 cavity.

Pyridylmethylamine linked to a phenyl-isoxazole-morpholine; pyridine N provides mild heme-coordination potential, but the morpholine oxygen and secondary amine linker keep overall lipophilicity modest.

Complex fused benzimidazole-pyridinone scaffold with a chlorophenyl-hydroxyethylamino side chain and a methylaminopiperidine; multiple aromatic/heteroaromatic rings with imidazole-type nitrogens give real heme-coordination and stacking potential despite several polar OH/NH groups.
